title: The Great Depression & the New Deal

pairs.cause: The stock market crashed in October 1929.
pairs.effect: Banks and businesses failed and millions of people lost their savings and jobs.
pairs.explanation: The crash wiped out wealth and confidence, triggering a deep economic collapse.

pairs.effect: People rushed to pull out their money, causing even more banks to collapse.
pairs.explanation: Bank runs spread the crisis as healthy banks were drained of cash.

pairs.cause: Severe drought and poor farming practices hit the Great Plains.
pairs.effect: The Dust Bowl forced farm families to abandon their land and migrate west.
pairs.explanation: Dust storms ruined farms, displacing hundreds of thousands of people.

pairs.effect: Franklin D. Roosevelt launched the New Deal to provide relief, recovery, and reform.
pairs.explanation: Widespread suffering led voters and FDR to demand bold government action.

pairs.cause: New Deal programs put people to work on public projects.
pairs.effect: The federal government took on a much larger role in the economy.
pairs.explanation: Washington began actively managing jobs, banking, and relief for the first time at this scale.

pairs.cause: Congress passed the Social Security Act.
pairs.effect: The U.S. created a safety net of retirement and unemployment benefits.
pairs.explanation: It established lasting federal support for the elderly, unemployed, and disabled.

pairs.cause: The New Deal expanded federal power and spending.
pairs.effect: Debates over how big a role government should play in the economy continue today.
pairs.explanation: The New Deal reshaped expectations of government in ways still argued over.
